### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 43 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **48** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a6dbd8c4389d59c6e56cab8fcbc7f927e92e4c32` — the merge of head `6cacf68c50645caa3d6d48817d03b877468e8d4a` into base `fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a6dbd8c4389d59c6e56cab8fcbc7f927e92e4c32 && git checkout a6dbd8c4389d59c6e56cab8fcbc7f927e92e4c32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 6cacf68c50645caa3d6d48817d03b877468e8d4a && git checkout -B drift-repro fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 && git merge --no-ff 6cacf68c50645caa3d6d48817d03b877468e8d4a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T19:39Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `b413fd243d02076c558002fa2a895b263f17f614`

Read against claim 6955512353 (seat route A) with its file-surface amendment 6958279133, and os-dev report 6958229650 on #34885.
- **Size:** 5 files, +519/-17.
- **Not governed:** `check-governed-merges --branch pr-34957` reports 0 of 5 paths and 536 lines.
- **CI at this head:** 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, all concluded.
- **Claim surface:** the middleware, the new helper `owner-anchor-stamp.ts` beside it, a new card-named test, the changeset, and `system-context.mdx` (amended). All 5 files are inside it.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** `Fixes #34885` is right. The card's repro (a private object, a non-admin action-body insert, then a 404 on `get`) is the first pinned case, with the same envelope's direct create as its control.
- **Where the stamp sits.** It runs ahead of the `isSystem` short-circuit. It is gated on `operation === 'insert'` plus `isActionBodyElevation` (`isSystem`, no `flowRunId`, and the `'action'` symbol mark from `@objectstack/core`) plus an object that carries `owner_id`. So a flow run (the flow wins over the mark, as in the identity-write refusal), a hook's `runAs: 'system'`, seed, boot and import, and a bare `isSystem` are all unchanged. The second ablation, which widens the predicate to `isSystem`, turns exactly those 5 cases red.
- **Same principal as a direct create.**
  - The stamp reads `opCtx.context.userId`, which is step 3.5's own `userId` (`:1839`). So under ADR-0090 D10 delegation it names the same principal, and that is pinned.
  - The guest is stamped with nothing (`isGuestEnvelope`), with `''` normalised to unset (ADR-0138 D1 item 5).
  - No payload value steers the stamp: a payload `created_by` is ignored. A client-spelt context has no symbol mark, so it is not the body's elevation, and that is pinned.
- **One rule in two places.** Step 3.5's inline `writesOwner` and the empty-owner stamp move into `owner-anchor-stamp.ts` unchanged: the own-property test, and park, then user, then guest normalisation. Step 3.5 now calls them, so the two readings cannot drift.
- **Seat rulings applied.**
  - An `owner_id` the body sets is kept, including another user's id, with no forge refusal. The body is trusted code, as before.
  - The queue rule follows the seat's confirmation. The row parks only when the body supplies `owner_id` empty beside a queue. An absent owner beside a queue is stamped, and the queue is the home queue. Both are pinned.
  - Batch rows are each stamped.
- **Ablations.** Removing the call turns 7 red (repro, control, empty, delegation, payload, batch, queue home). Widening the predicate turns 5 red. Both were restored by blob.
- **Docs.** `system-context.mdx` row 2 no longer claims an action body's insert is never stamped. That would have been the false published text, and the census row keyed `isActionBodyElevation` was regenerated, so `check:system-context-census` is green.
- **Changeset.** It is a patch on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` (a `none` kind takes patch). It names what stays unchanged and says that rows stored before this release keep `owner_id` null.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: The new path costs one `getObjectFieldNames` lookup per action-body insert, which is the same cached resolver step 3.5 uses. Other writes do not pay it.
- N2: An action run with no user principal (no `userId`, for example a service caller) is stamped with nothing, which is the same as step 3.5. I mention it only so that L2 sees it was considered.

Landing: not governed and green on this exact head. Because of `Clause-②: yes` (it changes who owns a stored row), it goes to the seat's fable L2 before area o3-G lands it. A later push owes a delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b413fd243d02076c558002fa2a895b263f17f614`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #34885 (body; triage 6953026994; claim 6955512353; os-dev-report 6958229650; amendment 6958279133), PR #34957 (body, 5-file list, net diff against `main` at base `fff0ad0c18`), L1-d ACCEPT 6958872123, and the 55 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read only to judge the diff (`app-automation-elevation.ts`, `engine-scoped-context.ts`, `engine-object-repository.ts`, `action-execution.ts#buildActionExecutionContext`, `flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts#elevationSource`, `security-plugin-object-inputs.ts#getObjectFieldNames`, `engine-insert.ts` and `assignment-rules.ts`, ADR-0142 D5).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public-surface change: an action-body insert now fills an EMPTY `owner_id` with the envelope's `userId`. Right, and it matches seat ruling A.** The stamp runs ahead of the `isSystem` bypass and is gated on `operation === 'insert'`, `isActionBodyElevation` and an object that has `owner_id`. `isActionBodyElevation` is `isSystem`, no `flowRunId`, and `appAutomationElevationOf === 'action'`. That is the same order `elevationSource` uses in the identity-write refusal (the flow wins over the mark), so the two readers do not drift. Flows, a hook's `runAs: 'system'` (re-marked `'hook'` by `withRunAs`), seed, boot and import writes, and a bare `isSystem` are unchanged. Test cases pin each of these, and ablation 2 turns exactly those 5 cases red.
- **Accept set: no write is newly refused. Right.** The new block only changes the payload and throws nothing. `getObjectFieldNames` catches its own errors and returns `null`, and a `null` means no stamp, so an unknown object cannot turn into a refused insert. A body-set `owner_id` (another user's included) is still kept without a forge guard, as before. No input that was accepted before is refused now.
- **Shared `owner-anchor-stamp.ts` against step 3.5: same rule, no drift. Right.**
  - `writesOwner` moved word for word: own-property test, not an array.
  - `hasEmptyOwner` is exactly the old inline condition: absent, `== null`, or `''`.
  - `stampEmptyOwner` keeps the old branch order: park → null, then userId → userId, then guest with `''` → null.
  - Step 3.5 now calls these three, and its behaviour is the same. The action path's `park` (queue column present, own non-empty `queue`, own empty `owner_id`) is step 3.5's grant-holder park. The only difference is that the action path does not resolve or admit the queue, and it never did, because of the system bypass. The owner rule is not affected.
- **Forge-proofing holds.**
  - The mark is `Symbol.for(...)` and has no JSON spelling.
  - The sandbox boundary is JSON in both directions, and `ObjectRepository.insert(data)` takes no context. So a body can neither forge the mark nor strip it, and a payload `created_by` does not steer the stamp (pinned).
  - In-process code (a code-registered hook, platform `sudo()`) could call the exported `markAppAutomationElevation`, or rebuild a context without the spread. Forging the mark only stamps the context's own `userId`, which is what step 3.5 stamps for that same envelope when it is not system. Stripping the mark only gives back the pre-fix null owner. Neither crosses a principal.
  - A client cannot reach `isSystem` at all.
- **MUST-FIX F1: the assignment-rule seam (ADR-0142 D5) is left unruled and undisclosed.**
  - `ObjectQL.insert` runs the security middleware, then the `beforeInsert` hooks, then `AssignmentRuleEvaluator.apply`. The seam routes only rows whose `owner_id` AND `queue` are both still empty (`engine-insert.ts` near `:1066`; `assignment-rules.ts` header: "a middleware-stamped owner is the acting user's own record").
  - Before this head, an action body's ownerless, queue-less insert on an object that `mayRoute` reaches was routed by the declared or organization-authored rules. At this head the middleware stamps the invoker first, so the seam stands down. That row now goes to the invoker instead of to the queue or member the rule picks.
  - There is also no spelling left that lets a body ask for routing. `owner_id: null` counts as empty and is stamped, and `owner_id: null` beside a queue parks in that queue, which the seam also skips.
  - That is parity with a direct create, which the seat's "mirror step 3.5" reading may well intend. But the claim, the dev report, its `open_questions`, the PR body, the changeset, the system-context row and L1 never name it, and no test pins it. ADR-0142's first consumer is intake routing (HotCRM cases and leads), and an action that logs a case or ticket is exactly that intake.
  - It is a change to who owns a stored row on routed objects, which is the contract question this face exists for. So it needs a seat ruling before landing, see ③.
- **Nit N-a: the `'action'` mark reaches more than the bodies the PR describes.** `buildActionExecutionContext` serves every handler an action door dispatches, a host code handler included (its own jsdoc), and `ObjectRepository.execute` marks `'action'` too. So a host code action handler's ownerless insert is now stamped with the invoker as well. The docs row is accurate (it keys on the mark), but the PR body and the changeset say only "an action body's `ctx.api`". This is disclosure only, and the effect is the same direct-create parity.
- **Nit N-b: a module header is now out of date.** `packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts`, outside the diff, still says the mark's "only reader narrows (it refuses; it admits nothing)". The new reader gives ownership. The header has no effect on correctness. Fix it in the push F1 already needs.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `'@objectstack/plugin-security': patch`. That is the only package the diff publishes. `content/docs` is not a package, and `owner-anchor-stamp.ts` is internal to the package: it is not added to `index.ts` exports in the diff.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`:** right on its own terms. No spec key, accepted value or metadata type changes, and `none` takes `patch`. ⚠ This depends on F1. If the seat rules that declared or authored assignment rules no longer reaching action-body inserts is a changed meaning for the `assignment_rule` metadata type, the kind becomes `semantic` and the level `minor`. The seat should say which, on F1's ruling.
- **Clause-②: yes (no arm) is the right word.** The change widens what the invoker ends up owning (read and update on rows that used to be unowned). It does not narrow the accept set: no caller's write that was accepted before is refused now. The queue-claim corner below does not change that.
  - A queue member's ADR-0142 D4 claim of a body-queued row with an absent owner was admitted before, because the row was unowned. It is not admitted now, because the row is the invoker's.
  - What changed there is the stored state the body produces, not the gate's verdict on the same input and state. The body keeps an explicit park spelling (`owner_id: null` beside the queue), and the seat confirmed this reading.
  - So this is not a `(narrowing)` declaration needing CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. F1 is the item that still has to be ruled.
- **Changeset body:** it names what stays unchanged and that there is no backfill. It does not name F1, and per N-a it says less than the mark reaches.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` (body-named queue, owner absent: stamp or park). Answered:** the seat confirmed option A (stamp; park only when `owner_id` is written empty beside the queue). The code and two pinned cases implement that. It still has to be re-read together with F1, because the queue reading and assignment routing interact. The seam skips a row with `queue` set either way, so A versus B does not change F1.
- **PR note 1 (no backfill). Acceptable.** A backfill cannot tell an action body's null-owned rows from guest, form or seed rows, which ADR-0138 D1 requires to stay unowned. `created_by` alone does not separate them. An administrator with the transfer grant can reassign. The changeset discloses it.
- **PR note 2 (an inherited hook context and `sudo()` inside the body are stamped too). Acceptable.**
  - The mark rides the spread by design (the core header, system-context row 1b).
  - `appAuthoredHookApi` and `sudo()` keep an existing `'action'` mark. Only `withRunAs('system')` re-marks it `'hook'`, which is not stamped.
  - A hook that inherits the context under a direct create is stamped by step 3.5 the same way, so this is parity.
  - The one asymmetry is platform `sudo()` code that runs under a body: stamped here, not under a direct create. It only fills an empty owner, and only with the invoker. Noted, not a finding.
- **L1 N1 (one cached `getObjectFieldNames` per action-body insert). Accepted.** A `null` result is not cached, so an unknown object re-reads each time. That is negligible and the same resolver step 3.5 uses.
- **L1 N2 (no `userId` means no stamp). Accepted.** Same as step 3.5.
- **Docs row (`system-context.mdx` row 2 and the regenerated register line `owner-anchor-stamp.ts#isActionBodyElevation | 1 | 2`). Correct as far as it goes.** It covers the key, the guest, a body-set owner and the queue park, and the census gate is green on the head. It needs F1's disclosure if the seat takes parity.
- **Out-of-surface edit (`system-context.mdx`).** It was declared and the claim was amended (6958279133). Fine.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The stamp is an in-memory write to the payload, and the only lookup is the cached schema read.
- **Escalation (F1) to the seat.** Rule one of:
  - (a) Parity with a direct create: action-body inserts are not routed by assignment rules. Then disclose it in the changeset, system-context row 2 and the PR body; pin a test with a routed object showing the seam stands down; and state the Metadata-protocol judgment (none or semantic) on the ruling.
  - (b) Leave rows an assignment rule may route to the seam, and stamp the invoker only when no rule claims the row. That needs an engine-side change outside the claimed surface.
  - Either way it is a new head, which owes a delta read.
- **CI on this head, polled to completion: 55 check-runs, 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending.**
  - Passed: Test Core 1–10, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check (all four lanes), Lint & Repo Gates (all lanes), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Build Docs, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the PR-body guards.
  - The skipped runs are opt-in, UI-lane or schedule-gated.
  - The queued suites from the claude, vercel, cloudflare, fly-io and objectstack-fleet apps have 0 check-runs and carry no verdict.
- **Merge standard (only nits may stay open): not met.** F1 is must-fix. N-a and N-b are nits and can go in the same push.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34885-action-insert-owner-stamp`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

I owe the record one admission: my first read missed the assignment-rule seam that L2 F1 found. The ruling settles it, and this delta answers it.

### What holds
- **F1, measured first as the ruling asked.** The new `describe` uses a private `abo_ticket` with a declared assignment rule that sends every unowned, queue-less insert to an org member:
  - Positive controls: a system insert and a flow run's insert (`isSystem` plus `flowRunId`) are both routed to the rule's user. So the rule really routes on this rig, and a flow is unchanged.

  - The changeset, `system-context.mdx` row 2 and the PR body each state that an action-body insert is the invoker's own record, like a direct create, so assignment rules route neither.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: A body that wants a rule to route its row has no spelling today. The changeset says so. If an app needs it, that is a new card (for example, an explicit routing request), not this one.

Landing: not governed. The seat's delta L2 comes next, then area o3-G lands it once CI is fully green on this exact head. `Check Changeset` was still in progress when I read it. A later push owes a delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6cacf68c50645caa3d6d48817d03b877468e8d4a`
Local-runs: none

This is a DELTA review over the seat's L2 FAIL record 6959079731 at head `b413fd24`, to head `6cacf68c`. It covers card #34885 (body and every comment: triage 6953026994, claim 6955512353, os-dev-report 6958229650, amendment 6958279133, seat ruling 6959099293, amendment 2 6959130385, fix-round report 6960222056), PR #34957 (body, 6-file list, net diff against `main`), L1-d ACCEPT 6958872123 and L1-d delta ACCEPT 6960315176, and the 74 check-runs on this head.
- **The delta:** `git diff b413fd24..6cacf68c` is one commit, `6cacf68c` (parent `b413fd24`), with no main merge in it. It has 4 files and +93/-5: the changeset, `system-context.mdx` row 2, the `app-automation-elevation.ts` header, and the test.
- **Unchanged since the FAIL record:** `owner-anchor-stamp.ts` and `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`.
- **Merge check:** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 6cacf68c` (main at `0465f4aa`) merges cleanly. Main's 8 commits since the merge base `c81f498b` touch the middleware and `action-execution.ts` only through #34811's `userMessage` caller threading, which does not affect the mark, the bypass or step 3.5.
- **Code read outside the diff, only to judge it:** `engine-insert.ts` (the D5 seam near `:1066`), `assignment-rules.ts`, `engine-object-repository.ts` `execute`, `engine-scoped-context.ts`, `action-execution.ts#buildActionExecutionContext` and `body-doors.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **F1 (must-fix at `b413fd24`): CLOSED by ruling (a), parity.**
  - **What the seam does.** The seam runs after `beforeInsert` hooks and before the write, whatever `isSystem` is. It writes `owner_id`/`queue` only on a row whose owner and queue are both still empty. So the outcome depends only on the row's state when it reaches the seam.
  - **Positive controls (the rule really routes on this rig).** The new `describe` runs on `abo_ticket`, a private object. A declared rule `abo_ticket_intake` sends every unowned, queue-less row to `usr_abo_lead`, an active member of `org_abo`. Two inserts reach the seam unowned and go to the rule's user:
    - a system insert under `org_abo`;
    - a flow run's insert under the invoker's own envelope (`{ ...INVOKER, isSystem, flowRunId }`).
